The cybernetic figure slowly turns his head to the right, his glowing blue eyes scanning the horizon, mechanical joints in his neck whirring faintly. The camera follows his gaze, panning across the rooftop to reveal the city beyond: a river of light winding between dark towers, a flying vehicle gliding past between the buildings, its lights streaking. He watches it pass, then his eyes narrow slightly. The camera settles on his profile against the city glow, distant hover traffic humming, wind gusting across the rooftop. No text, no black frames.

nodes.title: About the Negative Prompt
widgets_values:
## About the negative prompt

The negative prompt is a list of things you would rather not see or hear, such as flicker, extra fingers or background music.

**With this workflow's default settings it has no effect.** LTX-2.5 Distilled runs at a guidance (CFG) of 1.0, and at that setting ComfyUI skips the negative prompt entirely to save time.

It only comes into play if you raise a CFG value above 1.0 in the sampler settings. Sampling then takes roughly twice as long, and the distilled model is not tuned for higher guidance, so try it on a short clip first.

For most shots, steer the result from the main prompt instead. Describe what you want ("steady locked-off camera", "soft window light", "no music") rather than listing what you don't.

nodes.title: POSITIVE PROMPT | main text
widgets_values: Egyptian royal in blue-and-gold headdress and high collar, white dress with golden embroidery and armbands, desert, robot soldiers in formation left and right. She walks steadily forward, head held level and gaze fixed ahead—no dipping or lowering of the head. The camera performs a single, smooth push-in only: starting in a wider shot of her, the robots, and the desert, it moves steadily forward until she is in a medium or medium-close frame, then holds. She stops, posture and head still upright, and says: “The old gods are silent. I am not.” Robot soldiers shift or march in place; sand and fabric move with the wind. No pull-back; the only camera move is the continuous push-in.
